pins.title: Pack a headlamp, always
pins.sub: US clocks go back on Nov 1, so dusk comes an hour earlier. Keep a charged headlamp in your pack, even on short day hikes.

pins.title: Short steps on frost
pins.sub: Shaded slopes can stay icy long after sunrise. Slow down, take short steps and plant a pole before you move. Real ice needs traction.

pins.title: Down is the easy half
pins.sub: The park's advice: use 1/3 of your time going down and 2/3 climbing back out. Turn around early.

pins.title: Carry all your water
pins.sub: The taps at Bright Angel's Mile-and-a-Half and Three-Mile Resthouses run May through October. Fill up at the rim.

pins.kicker: Grand Canyon South Rim in winter
pins.title: Icy at the top
items: Pack warm layers for the rim
Allow extra time to climb out
pins.sub: Based on NPS advice for the Bright Angel Trail. Check nps.gov/grca before you go.

pins.kicker: Dad says hiking isn't for him?
pins.title: Invite him on an easy one
pins.sub: Pick a short, flat trail with a view and a snack stop. Our printable coupons turn that invite into a gift.

pins.title: When poles help most
items: Long days with a heavy pack
pins.sub: On short, flat walks, or scrambles where you need both hands, you can leave them home.

pins.title: Carry it upside down
items: Lid down: ice forms at the bottom
Pack it inside, near your back
pins.sub: Simple tricks to keep your water drinkable at the summit.
